findings.evidence: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean: `instance : CoeSort (IntegralLattice V) (Type u) := ⟨fun L ↦ L.carrier⟩`; same file line 73 already uses `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier` for `↥(L.carrier.prod M.carrier)`, and `orthogonalSum_carrier` is `(rfl)`. The pre-PR code assigned the identically-typed private `prodCarrierEquiv L M` directly to `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv`.
findings.fix: Delete the second paragraph and define `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv L M := Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier`; if the inline `where` block is kept for defeq reasons, state that reason instead of the module-structure claim.
findings.issue: The note "Unlike `Submodule.prodEquiv`, this targets the canonical integer-module structures on the lattice carrier types rather than the module structures inherited from their ambient submodules" is false: `↥L` *is* `↥L.carrier` (`instance : CoeSort (IntegralLattice V) (Type u) := ⟨fun L ↦ L.carrier⟩`, Basic.lean), so both carry the same `Submodule.module ℤ` structure and `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier : ↥(L.carrier.prod M.carrier) ≃ₗ[ℤ] L × M` is the same statement. The docstring tells readers a separate construction is required when it is not.

summary: Both new files carry accurate module docstrings and documented public declarations, and the Mathlib cross-references (`AddSubgroup.prodEquiv`, `QuotientAddGroup.prodAddEquiv`, absence of a submodule form upstream) check out. One added docstring in OrthogonalSum.lean states a false reason for re-inlining a definition.
